title: 58. Numeracy & Number Systems: Simplifying Square Roots of Integers
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate the square root of a perfect square integer.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{144}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(12^2=144\), the square root of \(144\) is \(12\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{144}=12\). The choice "\(72\)" is half of \(144\), which does not represent the square root.
questions.hint: Find a nonnegative integer whose square equals the number under the radical.

questions.concept: Simplifying Square Roots by Extracting Square Factors
questions.learningObjective: Simplify integer square roots by extracting perfect square factors.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{50}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(50=25\cdot2\). Then \(\sqrt{50}=\sqrt{25}\sqrt{2}=5\sqrt{2}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(5\sqrt{2}\). Squaring the alternative gives a different radicand.
questions.hint: Look for the largest perfect square factor of \(50\).

questions.concept: Simplifying Square Roots with Larger Radicands
questions.learningObjective: Simplify integer square roots by extracting perfect square factors.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{72}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(72=36\cdot2\). Then \(\sqrt{72}=\sqrt{36}\sqrt{2}=6\sqrt{2}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(6\sqrt{2}\). Squaring the alternative gives a different radicand.
questions.hint: Find the largest perfect square factor of \(72\).

questions.concept: Simplifying Square Roots with Multiple Square Factors
questions.learningObjective: Simplify integer square roots by extracting perfect square factors.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{200}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(200=100\cdot2\). Then \(\sqrt{200}=\sqrt{100}\sqrt{2}=10\sqrt{2}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(10\sqrt{2}\). The alternative does not preserve the radicand when squared.
questions.hint: Identify the largest perfect square that divides \(200\).

questions.learningObjective: Simplify and add two square-root expressions with the same resulting radical.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{18}+\sqrt{8}\).
questions.explanation: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}\) and \(\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}\). Adding like radicals gives \(3\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{2}=5\sqrt{2}\). The choice "\(\sqrt{26}\)" incorrectly adds the radicands.
questions.hint: Simplify each square root separately, then combine like radicals.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify and subtract two square-root expressions with the same resulting radical.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{45}-\sqrt{20}\).
questions.explanation: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt{5}\) and \(\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5}\). Subtracting like radicals gives \(3\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{5}=\sqrt{5}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(\sqrt{5}\). The alternative adds coefficients instead of subtracting them.
questions.hint: Simplify each square root, then subtract the coefficients of the common radical.

questions.concept: Simplifying Square Roots by Extracting Perfect Square Factors
questions.learningObjective: Simplify integer square roots by extracting perfect square factors.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{147}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(147=49\cdot3\). Then \(\sqrt{147}=\sqrt{49}\sqrt{3}=7\sqrt{3}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(7\sqrt{3}\). The alternative exchanges the extracted factor and remaining radicand.
questions.hint: Look for a perfect square factor of the radicand.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify and combine three square-root terms by adding and subtracting like radicals.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{32}+\sqrt{18}-\sqrt{50}\).
questions.explanation: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{32}=4\sqrt{2}\), \(\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}\), and \(\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt{2}\). Then \(4\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2}-5\sqrt{2}=2\sqrt{2}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(2\sqrt{2}\). The alternative combines the signed coefficients incorrectly.
questions.hint: Simplify each square root to a multiple of \(\sqrt{2}\) before combining.

questions.concept: Simplifying a Square Root with a Large Perfect Square Factor
questions.learningObjective: Simplify integer square roots by extracting perfect square factors.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{288}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(288=144\cdot2\). Then \(\sqrt{288}=\sqrt{144}\sqrt{2}=12\sqrt{2}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(12\sqrt{2}\). The alternative extracts only half the required outside factor.
questions.hint: Find the largest perfect square that divides \(288\).

questions.learningObjective: Simplify and combine three square-root expressions after extracting perfect square factors.
questions.question: Simplify \(\sqrt{108}-\sqrt{75}+\sqrt{48}\).
questions.explanation: Simplify each term: \(\sqrt{108}=6\sqrt{3}\), \(\sqrt{75}=5\sqrt{3}\), and \(\sqrt{48}=4\sqrt{3}\). Then \(6\sqrt{3}-5\sqrt{3}+4\sqrt{3}=5\sqrt{3}\). Therefore, the simplified form is \(5\sqrt{3}\). The alternative changes the signs of the last two terms, giving the coefficient sum \(6+5-4\) instead of \(6-5+4\).
questions.hint: Simplify each square root to a multiple of \(\sqrt{3}\), then combine the coefficients.
